title: Non-FIFO, FIFO, and causal ordering
summary: Compare channel guarantees and see why causal ordering requires buffering and message timestamps.
objectives: Distinguish random delivery from FIFO delivery

sections.title: Channel guarantees
sections.body: A non-FIFO channel can deliver messages in random order. FIFO preserves the send order for messages on the same channel. Causal ordering preserves the order of causally related sends when the messages are delivered to the same process.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Ordering questions test a guarantee boundary: FIFO is channel-local, while causal ordering follows the global happens-before relation between sends.

sections.title: Synchronization by delivery discipline
sections.body: Causal ordering provides built-in synchronization, but the receiver may need to buffer messages until earlier causal dependencies arrive. Timestamps make those dependencies observable.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The implementation cost explains why stronger delivery guarantees are not free: metadata, buffering, and release rules move into the system.

examples.title: Choose the weakest sufficient channel
steps: Ask whether order matters only per sender-channel.
If yes, FIFO may be sufficient.
If cross-process causal dependencies matter, require causal ordering.
If neither matters, do not pay for unnecessary metadata and buffering.
examples.answer: The guarantee should match the application invariant, not the strongest label available.

contrastDrills.prompt: Two messages sent on one channel must be delivered in send order. Which guarantee is needed?
contrastDrills.explanation: FIFO preserves the order of messages on the same channel; non-FIFO explicitly allows arbitrary delivery order.
contrastDrills.misconception: Name the ordering, time, or communication boundary before choosing.

contrastDrills.prompt: Which guarantee tracks causal order between sends that may originate on different processes?
contrastDrills.explanation: Causal ordering follows happens-before dependencies between sends, not merely one channel's queue order.
contrastDrills.misconception: Name the ordering, time, or communication boundary before choosing.

math.explanation: Causal ordering requires a receiver to deliver messages in an order consistent with causal precedence between their send events. FIFO is weaker because it only constrains one channel.
math.name: Causal-delivery guarantee
math.purpose: Use it to check whether delivery order preserves a known dependency between messages.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why is FIFO not enough to preserve every causal dependency?
criticalQuestions.angle: Compare messages sent by different processes with messages on one channel.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: FIFO preserves one sender-channel order. A causal dependency can cross channels and processes, so a stronger causal-ordering rule is needed.

criticalQuestions.prompt: What is the cost of stronger delivery ordering?
criticalQuestions.angle: Name the state needed to know whether a message is safe to deliver.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: The system may need timestamps, receiver buffers, and release conditions; stronger consistency moves metadata and waiting into the implementation.
